subject: Percentage vs fixed rebate structure and reseller margin review

Subject: Options for marketplace pricing cadence (percentage rebate vs fixed credit)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the per-call analytics. As we shape the private offer for CloudWave, procurement asked us to present two alternate pricing mechanics for their marketplace listing and reseller chain:

1) Percentage rebate (post usage): 12-18% rebate paid quarterly to CloudWave, with explicit reseller uplift sliced from Redwood's list price.
2) Fixed credit model: a fixed monthly credit applied to invoice (e.g., $X/month) regardless of usage, with a smaller explicit reseller commission on top (flat $/month or per-seat).

They want to understand:
- How each option affects partner-margin transparency (reseller netbacks)
- Which option better preserves price signal for end customers
- Any implementation differences for marketplace billing (commit smoothing, true-ups, invoice pathing)

Can you and your ops team sketch tradeoffs and an initial recommendation? Also, procurement asked for an example showing net revenue to CloudWave vs net to reseller under both approaches for a 12-month commit.

I'll attach a short template term sheet with our must-haves.

Thanks,

Hi Emily — thanks for sending the term sheet and the clear framing. Quick readthrough and initial thoughts below; Ben and Connor are looped to surface operational and partner-impact details.

High level recommendation (short):
- For larger, variable-usage customers we usually prefer the percentage rebate approach because it scales with consumption and preserves per-unit list price signals (helps downstream resellers avoid over/under-subsidizing customers).
- For customers with predictable monthly spend and simple reseller models, the fixed credit reduces billing complexity and is easier for finance to forecast.

Tradeoffs to include in the memo:
- Transparency: percentage rebate can be split into explicit reseller % and retained vendor % on the invoice; fixed credit often shows up as a line item discount which obscures unit economics unless we publish a separate breakdown to partners.
- Marketplace billing: percentage rebates require quarterly true-ups and a small reconciliation flow in our billing pipeline; fixed credits are applied as recurring invoice line items and are simpler for marketplaces that don't support post-invoice rebates.
- SLA/overage treatment: percentage works well with metered overages; credits can create edge cases for burst months (we can carve out overage handling).

Ask: Ben / Connor — can you draft an example 12-month proforma (two scenarios) showing: list revenue, rebate outflow, reseller commission, Redwood net, and the resulting reseller netback? Also note any downstream marketplace constraints on applying quarterly rebates vs monthly credits.

Emily — will follow with the proforma and a recommended clause for invoice pathing.

Emily / team — attached is a quick proforma snapshot (separate file) and operational notes. Key operational items:

- Implementation complexity:
  * Percentage rebate: requires 1) quarterly reconciliation job, 2) partner statements, 3) ability to issue negative adjustments to invoices in months with credits. Our billing engine supports this but the marketplace connector (AWS/GCP) may need a mapped reconciliation identifier.
  * Fixed credit: simply provision a recurring negative line item; marketplaces generally accept this if the private offer metadata includes a credit mapping.

- Partner margin transparency:
  * If CloudWave needs reseller netbacks to be visible to end resellers, we recommend combining percentage rebate with an explicit reseller commission line (e.g., 10% reseller, 6% vendor rebate) so reseller P&L remains clean.

- Escrow / reserve considerations:
  * For high-risk deals we can recommend putting 50% of the rebate into a short-term escrow that releases on confirmed usage milestones. This protects partners from over-crediting during onboarding months.

Hi Emily — following up on Ben's note with connector constraints and suggested term language.

Connector constraints (short):
- AWS Private Offer: supports list price + custom discounts; post-invoice rebates must be handled off-platform (we report credits back to AWS for reconciliation). Meaning: percentage rebate that pays out quarterly requires a parallel reconciliation and a settlement ledger. Recommend we include a clause: "Quarterly rebate settlement will be processed off-marketplace; Redwood will provide partner statements and a settlement invoice within 45 days of quarter end."

- GCP Marketplace: supports recurring credits more cleanly in private listings; fixed monthly credits can be applied as recurring adjustments. Still recommend a true-up clause for annual reconciliations.

Suggested term sheet language (blurb):
- "Rebate structure: Parties agree to either (A) Quarterly percentage rebate equal to X% of billed usage (subject to settlement and reconciliation) or (B) Fixed monthly credit of $Y applied to Redwood's invoice. Quarterly rebates will be settled by Redwood within forty-five (45) days of quarter end and documented via partner statements. Fixed credits will be reflected as recurring invoice adjustments and reconciled annually."

Next steps: Jasmine / Ben, we can bake the chosen structure into the term sheet Emily sent and provide the example proforma numbers for CloudWave to present to their finance team. Emily — if CloudWave prefers the percentage approach we'll provide a partner-facing netback table that shows reseller %, Redwood retained %, and expected gross-to-net timing.

Best,
